whatItDoes: Analyzes JavaScript and TypeScript code in the browser to estimate cyclomatic complexity, lines of code (total, code, comment, and blank), and a simple maintainability indicator. Highlights which functions are the most complex so you know where to refactor.
whyItExists: Complex code is harder to test and maintain, and it correlates with bugs, but it's hard to judge by eye. A quick complexity metric lets developers flag the riskiest functions and protect code quality before complexity becomes unmanageable.
whoShouldUse: Developers and tech leads performing code reviews, maintainers measuring technical and cognitive debt, and engineers deciding where to split or refactor functions.
useCases: Measure cyclomatic complexity of a module before a review
Find the functions with the highest complexity to target refactoring
Track complexity changes between refactors of a file
Get an at-a-glance maintainability score for a code snippet
Benchmark a legacy file before deciding whether to refactor or rewrite it
instructions: Paste your JavaScript or TypeScript code into the editor
The analyzer reads LOC counts and complexity automatically
Review the overall score for the snippet
Read the function-level breakdown to find the highest-complexity functions
Use the recommendations to plan your refactoring
Run it again after refactoring to confirm complexity dropped
examples: A function with 5 if/else branches and 2 loops → cyclomatic complexity ~8
A 20-line pure function with no branches → cyclomatic complexity 1
A module with many >10-complexity functions → the module is likely hard to maintain
LOC breakdown: 120 total, 95 code, 12 comments, 13 blank
bestPractices: Keep per-function complexity under roughly 10 to make each function easy to test
Use the metric as a signal for refactoring, not a hard law
Re-check complexity after each refactor to confirm it lowered
Combine complexity with readability and test coverage for a full picture
Investigate complexity outliers in code review before merging
commonMistakes: Treating high complexity as the only indicator of poor quality
Gaming the metric by splitting functions artificially
Ignoring nested conditionals that inflate perceived readability
Comparing complexity across unrelated languages or paradigms
Measuring a single file while ignoring how it couples with the rest of the module
faq: What is cyclomatic complexity? — A count of independent paths through a function, based on decision points like if, else, case, and loop.
What is a good complexity score? — Value 10 per function is a common guideline; lower is easier to test and maintain.
Can it analyze TypeScript? — Yes, it understands TypeScript syntax as well as JavaScript.
Is my code sent anywhere? — No, all analysis runs locally in your browser.
features: Total LOC, code, comment, and blank counts
